title: WebSec Campaign Plan
description: The contract between strategy and execution: the planner (LLM) proposes prioritized questions with trajectories and budgets; the deterministic orchestrator decides whether/when/where each stage runs. The plan is data, never a script the model executes.

required_context.description: artifact ids the specialist pass must be given

budget_class.description: cheap = local/static, standard = mid model, expensive = frontier model

closed_reason.description: WHY the priority was closed — required by the CLI for any closing status; 'answered' with no reason or evidence ref is the run-2 hole (Q-004 closed with a sentence instead of a probe)

closed_ref.description: evidence the closure rests on: a finding id (F-...), exec id (EXEC-...), artifact id, or file#L anchor. An 'answered' priority with no closed_ref is flagged in the report's answer-quality section

families.description: candidate families seeded from the model — the checklist a closure must attest against

families_checked.description: families the operator attested as compared/checked when closing

trajectory_matrix.description: enforces orthogonality: each trajectory gets its own perspective contract, and thin-coverage components get re-pointed

A-code.description: implementation-centric: bugs in the code as written

B-economic.description: assume the protocol is economically exploitable; find the imbalance

C-state-machine.description: find dangerous call/state sequences and illegal transitions

D-attacker.description: assume the attacker holds each realistic role; find role-abuse

E-historical.description: find variants of known exploits, patches and disclosures

F-integration.description: assume every external contract/token behaves unexpectedly

G-drift.description: spec vs implementation vs deployment vs config divergence

H-lifecycle.description: consensus/lifecycle game: the adversary WINNING the commit→challenge→finalize game
